newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Geneva private bank ups net profits 4.3 pct in 96.
newsitem.headline: Geneva private bank ups net profits 4.3 pct in 96.

text.p: Swiss private bank Union Bancaire Privee said on Tuesday it had increased net profits 4.3 percent to 161.3 million Swiss Francs in 1996 compared with the previous year.

In a rare announcement on financial results in Switzerland's secretive private banking hub, the Geneva-based bank said in a statement that assets under its consolidated balance sheet grew 6.1 percent to 13.41 billion Swiss Francs in 1996.

Union Bancaire Privee's consolidated income rose 11 percent to 449 million Swiss Francs over a year ago, but the rise in expenditure was higher at 23.9 percent to 205.7 million Swiss Francs because of an increase in investments.

The bank said 1996 was marked by expansion abroad and restructuring and consolidation at home. Investments abroad included the launch of an asset management operation in New York and the purchase of a stake in Brazil's Banco Excel Economico.
The statement gave no other details. The bank does not publish the volume of assets it manages.
Swiss private bankers estimate that assets under management in the industry grew by 15 percent in 1996, which they say was a good year in terms of return on investments and new cash flows.

There are no official statistics on the Swiss private banking industry but a recent survey by Credit Suisse First Boston bank put the volume of private assets under management in Switzerland at some $1.8 trillion.
